To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) natural resource dependence is associated with growth failure in developing countries, (2) the type of natural resources is important for the effect of dependence on growth, (3) the effect of natural resource dependence on growth is mediated by the institutional quality of the economy, (4) natural resource dependence has a negative effect on institutional development.
The curse of resource dependence is more general than the literature suggests.
the resource curse is not only a problem in mineral exporting countries but that all natural resource exporting countries are prone to growth failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of natural resource dependence on growth, and the mechanisms through which the curse operates.
the impact of natural resource abundance on economic development.
how the type of natural resources exported affects the growth performance of developing countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the natural resource curse exists, but it is a more complex phenomenon than the simple resource curse literature suggests.
natural resource dependence, especially the point-source type, is detrimental to growth and that it is a curse.
the curse exists, but its effects are not as strong as previously thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
natural resource dependence has been detrimental to economic development in the 1970s and 1980s, but the resource curse seems to have abated in the 1990s.
natural resource dependence, especially of a point-source type, has a negative impact on growth.
resource dependence, in general, has a negative effect on institutional development, and this in turn hampers growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
natural resource dependence is not a curse per se but a curse in the presence of institutional weaknesses, which are not confined to mineral exporting countries.
the curse is more general, not just confined to mineral exports.
natural resource dependence can be good for growth, but only if it is diffused.
